title: To Rake or Not to Rake? Excuses Michiganders Use to Skip It - NewsBreak
text:
By Kristen Matthews ,
1 hours ago There are so many things to love about fall in Michigan! The gorgeous colors, the scrumptious cider and donuts, the cozy sweaters, and even the spooky vibes.
But, there’s one thing that I truly hate about fall (and I know I can’t be alone in this), and that’s raking all the leaves.
The Michigan Leaf-Raking Debate Sure, I love seeing all the leaves change color, and it’s whimsical when they first start to fall. But, the inevitable clean up that follows is always annoying, to say the very least.
Photo by Wendell Shinn on Unsplash I will obviously clean my gutters of all the leaves, but the ones that fall on the ground bring me to the age-old question: to rake, or not to rake?
5 Reasons You Shouldn’t Rake Your Leaves For me and many other Michiganders, the answer is easy: absolutely not. But if you’re the type of person that needs an actual reason to not rake your leaves, here are five:
1. It’s Good for the Environment
Science is giving you an excuse to be lazy. Leaves are great for pollinators, act as a natural mulch, and help critters survive the winter.
Download the WITL Mobile App Now 2. They’ll Just Come Back Tomorrow
Oh, did you just spend three and a half hours on Saturday raking your leaves, bagging them, and taking them to the curb? Congratulations… you have to do it again Sunday morning because your neighbor’s tree just dropped a bunch of leaves.
READ MORE: That Ball of Leaves in Your Michigan Tree Isn’t a Bird’s Nest
3. Leaf Blowers are the Devil’s Hair Dryer
They’re loud and annoying and no one wants to listen to that for hours on end.
4. The Wind Takes Care of It
Don’t worry, we’ll have some 30 mph gusts come through and move those leaves off your lawn.
5. Winter is Coming
Literally. Why bother raking when the snow is just gonna cover it in a week’s time?
So when you spend your entire weekend raking and cleaning the yard, don’t come into work and complain about not enjoying your weekend. You could have chosen to NOT rake leaves. Instead, you chose poorly. Next time, just say you’re leaving it for the bees.
11 Reasons Why Fall is Michigan's Best Season Fall is clearly the most superior of all the seasons that Michigan has to offer. But if you still needed some convincing, check out these reasons why fall is Michigan's best season. Gallery Credit: Kristen Matthews Mizina 1. Fall Flavors Fall brings out awesome flavors that don't necessarily stick around all year long. liveslow 1. Fall Flavors Apple cider is the star of the show when it comes to classic fall flavors. Massonstock 1. Fall Flavors Basic or not, is it really fall without pumpkin spice flavor? Pumpkin spice is one of those yummy flavors that only comes out around this time of year. Lilechka75 1. Fall Flavors Whether you call is hot chocolate or hot cocoa, hot chocolate is definitely suited for fall! AntonioGuillem 2. Cooler Weather No more sticky, sweaty skin. Fall is the start of cooler and crisper weather. Foxys_forest_manufacture 3. Sweater Weather I could live in sweaters. Honestly, if all year long was "sweater weather" I wouldn't be upset. Is there anything better than throwing on a comfy sweater on a cool, crisp fall morning? moodboard 3. Hoodie Season Perhaps, the only thing on par with "sweater weather" is "hoodie season". Granted, they are the same exact time of year, but there's just something about being wrapped up in a hoodie and pulling that hood up against any blowing winds. Plus, the extra large pocket holds extra snacks at the tailgate. Anest 4. No Mosquitoes I don't about y'all, but my blood is basically an open bar at a mosquito wedding. No matter how much bug spray I have on, or even if I'm covered from head to toe, I always get eaten alive. This summer has been particularly bad, that's why I'm so looking forward to this fall... NO MORE MOSQUITOES! nyul 5. Football Season Grab your lucky jersey and get ready to cheer on your favorite team because football season is back! There's nothing quite like rooting on your team to victory while enjoying the company of good friends and delicious food. Antonio_Diaz 6. Tailgating Tailgating before watching your favorite football team take on their rivals is basically an American tradition. And what tailgate would be complete without food, drinks, and lawn games? ShriramPatki 7. Nature's Beauty Mother Nature is so amazing, especially during fall in Michigan. Don't just take my word for it; this is a picture of Tahquamenon Falls in Michigan's eastern Upper Peninsula. Just look at the beauty and majesty in the rainbow of tree leaves. This is just a fraction of the beauty that Michigan offers during the fall. Plan a trip along Michigan's Tunnel of Trees along route M-119 to see for yourself. Photoboyko 8. Cozy Season I can't wait until fall when the weather get cool enough to cuddle up on the couch and not sweat your butt off. Just grab your blanket, grab your slippers, and don't forget a mug of your preferred warm drink, and boom; comfy level 100 unlocked. 9. Heating Bill Goes Down Who doesn't like to save money? Fall is the chance to do it in Michigan. You don't need to have your heat or your cold air on; all you have to do is open up the windows and catch that breeze. And just watch those utility bills dip down during the fall months. David Hanlon 10. Fun Fall Exclusive Activities As with all seasons, there are certain activities that are better, or that can only be enjoyed during the fall months... like going to the cider mill. Fall is apple season, which means that the cider mills are in peak production of apple everything; cider, hard cider, pies, donuts, and more! ziss 10. Fun Fall Exclusive Activities Corn mazes are another fall exclusive activity. They're a great activity for younger kids or people who just don't want to get scared at haunted houses. bmcent1 10. Fun Fall Exclusive Activities Hay rides are another fall staple activity! Just sit back and get ready to relax with friends and take in the fall sites. Or, perhaps it's a spooky hayride, be prepared to get scared! Aaron Savage, Townsquare Media 11. Spooky Season Fall is just the start of spooky season. All fall long, you have the chance to get your pants scared off at haunted houses, or even just a scary movie. Ryan McVay 11. Spooky Season And what fall spooky season would be complete without Halloween? Costumes, candy, and scares are in store for all on Halloween. Lies Michiganders Tell Themselves About Fall Even those of us that say it's our favorite season are lying someway or another. Fahmi Fakhrudin/Unsplash PSL Are Better Than Apple Cider If pumpkin spice lattes were the superior choice, why aren't they available year round? You know who never leaves our side no matter the season? Apple cider, that's who. Mitchell McCleary/Unsplash It Doesn't Rain That Much Yeah, keep telling yourself that. One minute it feels like summer and the next minute you wish you wore that extra layer and brought your umbrella. Jeremy Thomas/Unsplash We Don't Mind Raking Unless you're a cute kid that enjoys jumping in the leaves, you definitely don't enjoy raking them. It's a never ending task. You just spent a couple hours raking and have to do it all over again because of the wind and rain. Alex Geerts/Unsplash We Love Wearing Layers Yeah, until work is over and you walk outside and it's hotter than heck out and you're trying to strip off those layers in the parking lot. Timothy Eberly/Unsplash Winter Isn't Coming I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but it is. You can't stop it no matter how hard you try. Clem Onojedhuo/Unsplash The Leaves Are Always Pretty Yeah, when they're dry and still hanging on the tree. Not when they're soaking wet and sticking to your boots like a piece of toilet paper when you leave the bathroom. Ben Hershey/Unsplash Fall Weather Exists This one hurts, but its so true. If we're lucky, we get a couple of weeks of that cool crisp fall weather. Fall mainly consists of cold winds, rain and sometimes snow. Dan Gold/Unsplash Not Having Enough Blankets That ladder rack you have leaning on your wall or basket in the corner with six blankets in/on it says otherwise. Massmiliano Latella/Unsplash The Bees Won't Bug Me at the Orchard I hate to break it to you, but bees don't know how to mind their own business. As soon you break open that jug of cider they're going to be on you like white on rice. Taylor Foss/Unsplash Pumpkin Carving Won't Take Long Unless you plan on doing some kind of basic pumpkin smiley, carving is going to take you at least an hour. Stop lying to yourself. Dan Burton/Unsplash The Apple Orchard Won't Be Packed You can tell yourself as much as you want on the drive there that you're going to be the only one but you know that's a lie. I can here it now, "Oh, I didn't expect it to be this busy." Yes, yes you did. Neonbrand/Unsplash Spooky Season Starts in September Does it really though? You can try your hardest to convince everyone that it does but the first day of fall isn't until the end of September and people will hold onto summer as long as they can. Josh Applegate/Unsplash I Won't Drink Too Much at the Tailgate Every person that's said this is a liar. Most of us have been here, I know I have. There's absolutely nothing wrong with it either as long as you don't drink and drive and find a safe ride home. Freestocks/Unsplash I Don't Need a Jacket Grab the jacket. You'll thank me and yourself later. Amin Hasani Missing the Smell of Bonfires Do you really though? Do you miss having to wash your hair three times to get the smell of bonfire out of it, because I know I don't. Each State Ranked by How Miserable Their Winters Are Winter can be pretty rough. However, some states have it easier than others. Find out which states have the most miserable winters and find out where Michigan shakes out on the list.
